content.thinking: I need to fix both claims, and the CF-1 factor needs correcting too. The "Gbac1" reference in step 1 is fine as it stands.

action_items.item: Make the spend-summary tests, including a case for a shopper with no purchases this month, a required check that must pass before any change to src/io_shop/spend_summary.py can deploy.

Require flags that route traffic to new code paths, such as monthly-spend-feature, to be ramped up in steps, starting only after the deploy carrying the code has run healthy, rather than switched on for most traffic when the code deploys.
Block monthly-spend-feature from being switched back on until a deployed revision carries the empty-month guard.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to page the on-call person.
Find out why the deployment platform's API server was unavailable during the incident, and restore a working rollback path for io-shop.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed with server errors, and the account page error rate rose well above its usual level.
Account page requests failed because the spend summary raised a division-by-zero error inside average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 65279ee (P1): with it in place, account pages were logged as rendering normally and the account page error rate was at its typical level before the onset.

causal_chain.step: Requests reached that function because feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at P3. Flag evaluations went from all off before the onset, to a mix of off and on in the onset minute, to all on from the next minute. render_spend_summary sends a request to that function when the monthly summary is selected and the typical-spend rollout is not. The deploy of revision 383534e at P2 came at the same instant, so the record does not rule it out; the next step covers it.

The flag sent requests into code that could not serve a shopper with no purchases this month: the revision deployed at P2 (read at T10 as running on every replica) had taken out the empty-month guard, so the function divides the month's total by the count of purchases recorded this month with nothing to handle a count of none.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A software update took out the protection for shoppers who had bought nothing so far this month, so when a new account-page feature was switched on, the page's monthly spending calculation failed for those shoppers.

contributing_factors.factor: monthly-spend-feature was switched on at the same instant the revision carrying the changed code behind it was deployed. Most evaluations were already on in the onset minute and all were on from the next minute. No gradual ramp was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Had the flag been ramped up in small steps after the deploy, only a small share of account-page requests would have reached the failing function before the errors were noticed, which would have limited the harm.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test for a shopper with no purchases this month was seen in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py at the deployed revision. The change that removed the empty-month guard shipped without any seen check catching that the function now fails for that shopper.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test of the empty-month case would have failed against revision 383534e, and the guard's removal could have been caught before the deploy.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

got_lucky: The failing code path sat behind a feature flag that changed at the same moment as the deploy. Reverting the flag, which did not depend on the unreachable deployment platform, was enough to stop the errors.

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent placed the onset in the minute the deploy and the flag switch both landed, which tied the incident to those changes.
Argus moved on to the flag candidate C2 as soon as the rollback for C1 could not be taken, rather than waiting for the deployment platform.
The Mitigation Agent reverted monthly-spend-feature from ON to OFF. This needed nothing from the deployment platform.
The Mitigation Agent checked the service and judged the flag revert confirmed.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request for a person to review.

went_wrong: The first action tried, rolling back the io-shop deployment, could not be taken: the deployment platform's API server was unavailable, which also put restarting, scaling and every other platform action out of reach.
No on-call person was paged for the alert.

input.root_cause: Revision 383534e removed the guard in average_spend_per_item_this_month that handled a shopper with no purchases this month. It also changed the function to decide 'this month' from each purchase's recorded_at. The function now divides the month's total by the number of purchases recorded this month with nothing to handle an empty month, so it raises ZeroDivisionError for any shopper with no purchase recorded this month.
input.still_at_risk: Revision 383534e, which has no empty-month guard, was still running, so switching monthly-spend-feature back on would send account-page requests from shoppers with no purchases this month into the same division-by-zero failure.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
